_readme: Copy this file to repo-profile.json (same directory) and fill it in. It is the ONLY file
that teaches the pipeline about your repository — the workflow script itself is meant to
stay byte-identical across repos, so if you are about to edit the script, check whether a
The values below are an illustrative Node/TypeScript setup. Replace every one of them.
The bundle README has a per-stack command table (Node, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Make).
Underscore-prefixed keys are comments and are ignored.
_toolchain: build_verify_cmd and test_cmd are REQUIRED: the run refuses to start without them,
because a gate that executes nothing reports green. restore_cmd is optional (skipped
when empty). format_cmd/lint_cmd back the QA gate; use the same command twice if your
formatter has no separate check mode.
Every command must be non-interactive, must exit non-zero on failure, and must run from
the repository root.
The last three keys are OPTIONAL SPEED KEYS. Each falls back to its full-fat sibling, so
leaving them out is always safe — you just pay the slower command. They exist because the
inner loop dominates: an implement pass builds and tests once per pass per phase, and on
one measured .NET repo the whole-suite sweep was 16-25x running just the affected test
project. test_scoped_shape is the one worth filling in; the other two are minor.
build_fast_cmd     A build that skips codegen, doc generation or packaging that your
full build does. WARNING: if your fast build assumes generated
sources already exist, it only works after a full build has run —
setup runs build_verify_cmd once for exactly that reason, and the
pass prompt tells agents to re-run the full build if they hit a
missing-generated-source error. Omit if your build has no such mode.
test_no_build_cmd  Your test command with its implicit rebuild disabled, used by the
Test gate, which runs immediately after the Build gate on the same
tree. Omit if your test runner does not build, or has no such flag.
test_scoped_shape  A TEMPLATE, not a runnable command: how an agent runs ONE test
project/file/pattern. Use <placeholders>. Agents fill it in for the
code they just touched. Omit and they are asked, in prose, to scope
the full test_cmd down themselves.
_conventionsDoc: Repo-relative path to your binding conventions doc. EVERY implement and review agent is
ordered to read it in full and treat it as binding, so this is the highest-leverage file
in the whole setup. Start from conventions.template.md in this directory.
It must be COMMITTED — agents read it inside a fresh worktree.
_archDoc: Optional. An architecture/overview doc agents read before coding. Leave as "" if you
have none; the prompts adapt rather than referencing a file that does not exist.
_domainReviewer: Charter name of your repo-specific hazards reviewer, always on the review board.
reviewer-domain-hazards.md and keep it nearly empty until retrospect fills it.
_qaExtraSteps: Checks your build and formatter do NOT catch, run by the QA gate in order. Each entry is
one instruction — a shell command, or a prose check an agent can perform. Leave [] if
you have none. Examples: a type-check separate from the build, a dead-import sweep, a
generated-file drift check, a dependency audit.
qaExtraSteps: npx depcheck --json (report unused/missing deps introduced by this branch; do not remove deps used only at runtime)
_testFilterNote: Optional caveat appended wherever test_cmd is shown to an agent. Use it for the traps a
newcomer to the repo would hit: which suites the filter excludes and why, whether a
container runtime or service must be running, expected runtime. Leave "" if none.
testFilterNote: This command runs the unit suite only; the e2e suite needs a running database and is excluded on purpose.
